desert_p21_001.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_001.text: The courtyard's bitter plum tree leaned over the wall with an ambition the landlord did not share. He had trimmed the branches twice and still found fruit in the drain after every wind. Yue arrived carrying the household's agreed inventory sheet and found him on a ladder, arguing with a branch. The carpenter below asked him to come down before the doorway work began. He descended reluctantly and pointed to the fruit as though it had breached the lease. The niece, visiting before her aunt's transfer, tasted one and made a face.

desert_p21_002.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_002.text: The older woman had been right: it would need an heroic amount of sugar to become preserve. Only two rooms were changing use. The former merchant office stood vacant; the landlord's own storage room would become the companion's room after his boxes moved to his retained shed. The third room's regular tenant stayed under his existing terms, with his shared passage and wash times preserved. Nobody was being pushed out to make an emergency look generous. The tenant, a lamp repairer, inspected the planned threshold ramp and asked whether it would narrow his cart line.

desert_p21_003.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_003.text: The carpenter adjusted the position within the measured doorway width. A small practical revision made the patient route and the tenant's ordinary route fit the same gate. Yue wrote the actual arrangement in the signed house copy. The niece inspected the companion's room and found one cupboard too high for her painful shoulder. She asked the landlord to move its daily-use shelves lower before the lease began. He said his boxes had never complained. She said she was not leasing as a box. The lamp repairer laughed from the doorway and offered a spare low shelf for a modest price.

desert_p21_004.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_004.text: The landlord agreed to the fitting, the family to the shelf purchase. Yue carried the light shelf pieces while the carpenter handled the fastenings. The room acquired an arrangement the occupant could actually use rather than a handsome cupboard that invited her to injure herself reaching it. The wash corner had town service water through the courtyard's ordinary maintained connection, with its charge included to the stated lease allowance and additional use billed transparently. The drain led away from the patient threshold and remained clear.

desert_p21_005.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_005.text: Bao inspected the clean storage and receiving arrangement with the clinic social clerk before approving it as suitable for the planned recovery stay. It was a dwelling, not a new ward staffed all day. Qualified follow-up remained at the clinic, with scheduled visits and a transfer contact for changed symptoms. The daughter understood the distinction. She wanted a room where her mother could live between care, not a room required to pretend it contained every clinician.

desert_p21_006.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_006.text: The small ramp was built from sound material at the carpenter's ordinary rated capacity for the clinic carrier and attendants, its supports seated firmly, surface secure against slipping. The doorway's clear width allowed the entire stretcher through without tilting the supported leg. Bao and the receiving clerk watched an unloaded carrier test, then the carpenter checked the full expected load configuration using the clinic's stated rating rather than the niece standing in for a patient. The landlord grumbled that his old office had never needed such attention.

desert_p21_007.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_007.text: The lamp repairer said the old office had also never complained about the plum tree. This made the landlord consider his former tenant more fondly than before.

desert_p21_008.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_008.text: The patient chose the bed position from Yue's plain room drawing. She wanted the court visible through the wide door and the morning light away from her eyes. Her daughter arranged the actual bedding accordingly after the household market bundle arrived under its receipt. The niece checked that the support arrangement matched the clinic's instruction and kept the walking line clear. A bowl for small belongings went within easy reach. The onion basket stood farther away, where it would not tempt the patient to stretch or lean after it.

desert_p21_009.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_009.text: Yue brought the garden flower from the ward only after the woman agreed. It travelled in its little paper wrapper, a fragile thing whose whole journey could be made by two careful hands. The transfer followed the resident clinician's actual review. The older woman's injury remained supported, with no new finding requiring an altered immediate plan. She could leave the ward for suitable assisted lodging while continuing prescribed non-weight-bearing care and scheduled monitoring; that did not mean the suspected fracture had healed.

desert_p21_010.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_010.text: A qualified escort accompanied the low town cart, whose carrier supports and restraints were checked for the short journey. The niece rode in the approved companion place. Yue walked with the daughter, carrying only the light personal bundle. The ward door closed behind them without a triumphant flourish. The patient looked up at the strip of moving sky and said it was an improvement already.

desert_p21_011.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_011.text: At the courtyard gate the lamp repairer had moved his handcart out of the shared line, as agreed. The carpenter inspected the ramp once more before the carrier approached. The escort and attendants brought the patient through on the coordinated level movement they had planned, with no improvised lift over a narrow sill. Bao met them for the receiving arrangement and checked the supported leg after transit. The daughter set the mirror where it showed the tree and a patch of court. The older woman studied the reflection, then declared the wall less offensive from this angle.

desert_p21_012.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_012.text: The landlord, listening outside the door, looked unexpectedly pleased to receive a compliment meant mostly for a mirror. The niece wanted to unpack everything at once. Bao suggested she unpack the things needed before supper and let other work wait. The shoulder still deserved the gradual plan. Yue placed the lighter bundles where the niece directed, then stopped when the task was done. The daughter had a bakery shift later and arranged the evening visit honestly around it. The patient complained that everyone had calendars now.

desert_p21_013.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_013.text: The niece pointed to the recovery review and said a calendar was better than asking every morning whether the leg would be persuaded today. The woman had no answer strong enough to outargue that. She picked up the small bowl and inspected its crack instead.

desert_p21_014.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p21_014.text: This is your room, and the care plan is here so you can live in it. The supported leg stays under its prescribed arrangement. You have the review date, the changes that require us to be called and the actual clinic contact. Your companion is not expected to diagnose you or lift you alone. The household can share ordinary meals and visits without making every visitor an attendant. If the current support becomes uncomfortable or something changes, say it early. We can adjust care.

desert_p21_015.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p21_015.text: We do not need you to protect us from inconvenience by waiting until the problem has become harder to manage.

desert_p21_016.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_016.text: The older woman asked whether she could supervise plum preserve from the bed. Bao said supervision was not in itself a prohibited load, though the people doing the cooking might object. The niece objected immediately to acquiring a preserve business before she had found the washing cloths. The patient waved away the business and requested one small experimental pot later. Yue laughed, and the landlord appeared with three fallen plums as if he had been waiting for a use. The niece said later again. He set the fruit on the high outside bench and accepted the postponement.

desert_p21_017.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_017.text: In the room, the woman finally relaxed enough to sleep while the court continued without her directions. Han paid a visit after the patient had rested, bringing the closed expedition account copy the household was entitled to see. The emergency water transfer and transport facts were there, private clinical details elsewhere. She thanked him for the carriage and asked how his mother was. He looked surprised by the turn, then gave a simple household answer with no diagnosis. The daughter offered him tea from their own courtyard service arrangement.

desert_p21_018.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_018.text: He drank while the patient inspected the signature on the water entry. She said three hundred litres sounded both large and small. He said it had been exactly large enough to change what the cart could do, and still small enough that the well needed work.

desert_p21_019.speaker: han_xun
desert_p21_019.text: The cargo collection is settled. The later conservation trip has its own funding and schedule. Your household is not holding either job together by owing me a favour. The transfer account states why the shared emergency stock was used, and the cooperative accepted that use under the terms already agreed. I would still like to hear if the receiving arrangement failed you somewhere, because that is how the next hire improves. You do not have to tell me a pleasing rescue story. If you have one, my daughter will enjoy it.

desert_p21_020.speaker: han_xun
desert_p21_020.text: If you have a complaint, I can carry that just as readily, though she may say my handwriting has suffered.

desert_p21_021.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_021.text: The patient had one complaint: the cart canopy had shaded her eyes well but hidden every landmark she wanted to see. Bao explained why the shade and driving view had taken priority during transit. Han wrote the complaint anyway as a design question for future patient carriage, not a finding that the emergency arrangement had been wrong. The daughter asked whether a small side flap could be adjusted safely. The driver would have to assess it. The conversation ended with a practical possibility and no promise to rebuild a cart by next morning. The older woman seemed satisfied.

desert_p21_022.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_022.text: Her complaint had remained a complaint rather than become evidence of ingratitude. Tuo came the next day after her clinician's review extended ordinary level walking within the recovered ankle's comfortable range. She still avoided the long rough carrying work she had not been cleared to resume. In the court she met the lamp repairer struggling with a seized latch and offered no guide's advice about metal. He offered no lamp man's advice about her foot. They talked instead about the best tea stall nearby. Yue liked the ease of a conversation that did not recruit everybody into the other's profession.

desert_p21_023.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_023.text: Tuo sat by the patient's doorway and gave a richly exaggerated account of Du trying to buy the wrong ginger. The patient enjoyed it even knowing the exaggeration.

desert_p21_024.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p21_024.text: He is on the road with a conservator who makes him breathe away from pages. I regard that as a public benefit. Gao will keep the current route and old grades separate, the mason will stop them climbing what has not earned a foot, and the drivers will want to go home. Between them I expect a tolerable report. I also expect Du to return with three words he believes explain the universe, and I shall require him to say them after supper. Your courtyard has a better chair than mine used to.

desert_p21_025.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p21_025.text: If I praise it too loudly, my neighbour will send her nephew here to improve it until it breaks.

desert_p21_026.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_026.text: The niece went to the latch workshop for her first short paid sorting session only after the clinic cleared that ordinary level of work. The tasks used the arm comfortably, without heavy lifting or the provoking reach. She sorted small plates by marked size, stopped at the agreed time and earned the stated amount. When she returned, she had a black smear on her thumb and an opinion about workers who stored unlike pieces in one tray. Her aunt recognised the complaint from onion sorting and seemed delighted by its new setting.

desert_p21_027.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_027.text: Yue helped wash the plain work cloth, then let the niece show the wage entry herself. It was small, actual money, not a rescued person's honorary opportunity. The daughter changed one bakery shift so she could attend the next clinical follow-up, paying the trade in a later evening rather than pretending time appeared freely when family needed it. The niece would cover ordinary company, not medical decisions. The lamp repairer agreed to keep his cart out of the gate at the appointment hour and complained that the schedule would make him punctual for the first time in years.

desert_p21_028.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_028.text: The landlord gave him a doubtful look. They were becoming neighbours around the practical detail of a wide doorway. Yue copied the appointment on the house calendar and watched the daughter put it below rent, bread and the niece's workshop hours. The young worker visited with his reduced finger dressing and the school enquiry result. He had passed the basic reading portion, while the grant and practical entry steps remained. The older woman told him to stop holding the paper as if wind might steal the school. He relaxed his hand and sat on the outside bench.

desert_p21_029.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_029.text: The niece described the latch trays, and he confessed he had never thought tiny pieces could involve so many ways to be wrong. They compared work, laughing at their own certainty before the visit. Yue sat beneath the plum tree listening. Beyond the wall, a seller called ripe melons in a tone no bitter plum could honestly imitate. A gust brought three small plums down at once. One struck the young worker's shoe and bounced beneath the bench. The patient saw it and reached instinctively, then stopped when the support reminded her what movement meant today.

desert_p21_030.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_030.text: She called for the niece rather than pretend the pain had taught her a new kind of flexibility. The niece retrieved the fruit and put it in the outside bowl. The moment was so small that no one turned it into applause. Yue watched the old woman's hand settle around her own cup. Independence here was sometimes asking for the thing early enough that it could be handed over without another accident. The temporary-room lease's review date remained visible on the calendar.

desert_p21_031.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_031.text: The family's longer contribution, possible district extension and the patient's recovery plan would be considered before the initial support expired. The unresolved historic well account was not being spent in advance as rent. Han helped the daughter understand the receiving forms during a paid advice hour she chose, then left her to submit them herself. The landlord appreciated the clear schedule because he had bills too. When a neighbour called the courtyard a charitable lodging, he said it was a properly rented house. The patient laughed from inside and asked whether properly rented houses could still provide better cushions.

desert_p21_032.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_032.text: Bao's pilot treatment-room preparations continued in the grass village under the approved conditions. The hired carpenter fitted the work surface and screened storage; the responsible source arrangement was checked against the village's current service rather than Onion Hollow's reopened well by association. A municipal transfer agreement named the route and receiving clinic. The attendant learned ordinary cleaning and intake duties in town before moving to the staffed days. Bao inspected the actual prepared room with the board's representative and accepted the first limited opening dates. She returned carrying the signed condition sheet and looked exhausted.

desert_p21_033.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_033.text: Yue offered supper, not a new grand proposal. Bao accepted soup and sat down heavily in the first sound chair.

desert_p21_034.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p21_034.text: The shelf is cleanable, the water arrangement real, the transfer contact answered and the attendant knows when to call me instead of offering an opinion. Those are good beginnings. I wanted the room to open with every possible thing already solved, which is another way to ensure it never opens. The pilot has a narrow staffed schedule and a review after the first weeks. We can learn from actual use without telling people there is a hospital where there is a treatment room. I am frightened of doing too little.

desert_p21_035.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p21_035.text: I am more frightened of naming more than I can provide. Tonight I intend to do exactly enough eating and then sleep.

desert_p21_036.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_036.text: Yue walked Bao to the corner and saw her turn toward her own room, no longer trying to revisit the clinic out of habit. The street held the last warm light of the day. A pottery seller was stacking bowls inside bowls, making a soft hollow music. The smell of bread came from the bakery where the patient's daughter had taken her changed evening shift. Yue bought a heel loaf for tomorrow and tucked it into the habitual pack. She could have invented several errands to keep the day important.

desert_p21_037.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_037.text: Instead she returned to the courtyard only for the agreed short visit and found the patient arguing with her niece about the exact amount of sugar a bitter plum deserved. The preserve experiment used one small pot and the landlord's fallen fruit, with sugar bought by the family and cooking done by the daughter when her shift allowed. The patient supervised from bed, issuing opinions the cooks could decline. The first taste was too sharp. The second had enough sugar to make the niece accuse it of being a sweet pretending to be fruit.

desert_p21_038.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_038.text: The lamp repairer volunteered a third opinion and was awarded a spoonful. He approved, perhaps because he wanted more. Yue tasted the final small portion and felt a sting of sourness beneath the sweetness. The patient was pleased. It tasted like the courtyard's tree, which was what she had wanted.

desert_p21_039.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_039.text: A scheduled conservation message arrived while the pot cooled. The six-person team had reached the relay under the fresh access assessment and begun supported work within the cleared near room. Current source conditions remained under the keeper's maintenance; the visiting team had added no well water to its own stock. The conservator had found several top sheets readable in place and a subset suitable for supported transport under public custody. Other materials would remain condition-limited. Gao's note named the known next receiving date rather than promise a daily message.

desert_p21_040.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_040.text: Du's line to the apprentice asked for a dry shelf prepared in the municipal handling room, a real task attached to a real possible arrival. The apprentice took the shelf request to the responsible clerk and obtained the actual preparation appointment. She did not clear her own office cabinet as if the old material belonged to Du. The clerk appreciated the restraint and asked her to help compile the modern source wrapper under paid time. She accepted, pleased by work with a consequence beyond making somebody's prose fit a page.

desert_p21_041.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_041.text: Yue carried the empty clean wrapper supplies from the reading house under their receipt, then returned the borrowed basket. The papers they hoped to receive would arrive later if the field condition allowed. Today the town had made a proper place for them, with no need to pretend they were already here.

desert_p21_042.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_042.text: The courtyard's first quiet evening came after all visitors left. Yue stayed only to wash the cups she had used, then watched the daughter pull the door halfway so the patient could see the tree without receiving every passer-by's eye. The niece checked the ordinary support arrangement and sat with a piece of paid workshop sorting practice. Across the court, the lamp repairer closed his tools; the landlord hung a cloth over the plum bowl. Water ran briefly through the wash corner and stopped.

desert_p21_043.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_043.text: The room's lease, care and family schedules were all real, and none needed to be announced every time somebody breathed. The older woman settled into the sound of a house. On her way home Yue passed the public receiving board where the conservation team's next expected date was written beneath the current route warning. She checked it once and left it there. The six travellers had an actual return provision; the three former garden workers had town care and choices of their own; the well had reopened under its community's maintenance.

desert_p21_044.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_044.text: Here in Bitter Wells, a courtyard now held someone who could complain about a tree because she had a place to remain beside it. Yue did not draw a map of that small achievement. She remembered the wide door, the sour preserve and the patient asking whether the landlord would mind another bowl next season. The younger guide from the first rescue visited in a hired low town chair, its attendants keeping to the clinic's permitted transfer and her own recovery limits.

desert_p21_045.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_045.text: Her mother came beside her carrying the blue shawl, which the warm afternoon did not require but habit still recommended. The guide could not yet return to long uneven road work. She had accepted a bounded paid task checking local route accounts from home, using the corrected cards and her own observations with their dates. At the courtyard she asked where to put the chair so nobody had to pretend a leg existed in less space than it did. The niece liked her immediately.

desert_p21_046.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_046.text: The two injured women compared the indignities of shade covers, awkward cups and people who asked whether they were grateful before asking whether a pillow hurt. Their mothers and daughters, at different ages and roles, listened with varying degrees of defensiveness. Yue was asked to defend the caravan canopy. She said the driver needed to see and Bao needed the patient shaded, then conceded that a better adjusted side flap might help future carriage. The first guide laughed and said that was exactly the kind of answer she had begun giving paying clients.

desert_p21_047.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_047.text: The courtyard felt briefly like a professional conference in which almost everyone had brought an inconvenient leg. The younger guide's partner had arranged the maker's inspection of their handcart under the quarry custody record. The wheel and handle could be repaired, while the damaged axle required replacement rather than an optimistic binding. They would fund the work before the guide resumed the route, on her clinician's schedule, not sell the cart impulsively because the accident had made it frightening. The older woman listened and asked whether the new axle would make them happy.

desert_p21_048.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_048.text: The guide said it would make the cart useful. Happiness would need other arrangements. Her mother adjusted the unused shawl on the chair arm and looked pleased with that plain distinction. Yue returned the first guide's modern shelf-route copy, which she had borrowed for the cooperative correction account. Its owner checked the wrapper and put it with her own notebook. The older partner's recovered leather field book remained with him; the woman's notebook had come from her mother at home. None of these objects belonged to Lin because she had held them during the rescue.

desert_p21_049.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_049.text: The guide asked whether Yue planned more desert work. Yue said she was considering the next actual choice rather than choosing a whole future from a courtyard bench. The woman nodded and said she might try doing the same, once people stopped asking for her plans before her leg was ready. The visit ended before both patients became tired enough to mistake fatigue for irritation. The hired attendants moved the younger guide's chair along the clear passage under its ordinary load and width arrangement. The mother tucked the blue shawl securely away from the wheel.

desert_p21_050.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_050.text: Yue watched them leave and felt the first rescue's continuation in a quieter shape: paid home work, a cart maker's report, medical limits still respected. The older patient asked the niece whether there was any preserve left. There was one small spoonful. She ate it slowly and said the other guide had better come again when they had more than sour plums to offer.

desert_p21_051.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_051.text: Auntie Reed arrived in town for the market with her grandson on their own paid wagon space and provisions. She had brought mats, not an expedition rescue signal, and intended to sell them before the heat emptied the street. Yue found her at the receiving yard bargaining with a buyer who praised quality until asked to pay for it. The grandmother sent the grandson to count the unsold bundles and used the praise as a reason to hold her price. The buyer eventually bought two.

desert_p21_052.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_052.text: Yue waited until the coins were counted, then invited her to the courtyard if her schedule allowed. Auntie Reed said a woman with a well story ought to hear another.

desert_p21_053.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_053.text: At the courtyard, Auntie Reed inspected the tiny plum preserve with more suspicion than she had given the expedition's route sketch. The patient offered a taste and warned it was almost finished. The mat maker said almost finished was how the best things usually reached her. They spoke about the Blue Tap roof store, the Onion Hollow well and the difference between an office closure and the work people kept doing afterwards. Their accounts were specific: outlets cleared, ropes replaced, lids checked, children kept off bad edges. Du's absence spared him several remarks about clean map symbols.

desert_p21_054.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_054.text: Yue listened while the grandson tried to draw the crooked willow he had heard described, producing a tree shaped like a bent cart handle.

desert_p21_055.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_055.text: The grandson wanted to show his drawing to Du's apprentice. Auntie Reed agreed if he first carried the sold mat receipt to the receiving clerk, because public lessons did not relieve a child of every ordinary duty. He completed the errand and went with Yue to the office during its open hour. The apprentice gave him a scrap from the rejected proofs and showed how to start a tree from its trunk rather than every leaf. She had no time for a whole lesson, and said so. He accepted the brief instruction and drew the trunk again.

desert_p21_056.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_056.text: This one bent more naturally. He wrote his own name in a corner before the leaves could take all the remaining paper. The apprentice admired the improvement and directed Auntie Reed to the actual public drawing-session notice at the school. The next term's fee and dates were printed there. No immediate apprenticeship had been promised. The grandmother took the notice, calculated the market journeys it would require and told the boy they would discuss it at home. He looked disappointed, then noticed that discussing was better than refusing.

desert_p21_057.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_057.text: Yue gave him back the drawing without adding her own offer to pay. The grandmother had a household and a view of its future, neither of which needed to disappear because a visitor liked the child's tree.

desert_p21_058.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_058.text: At the receiving yard, the grass village's crop claimant confirmed her hearing date for the following week. Auntie Reed knew the field and agreed to provide her own dated observations if summoned through the collective. She would not speak for the whole crop from a glance at one row. The woman wanted a witness more than a promise, and accepted the distinction. Han arranged the paid travel provision specified for the hearing, with the exact receiving point written on the notice. Yue saw the two women fold their papers into different household wrappers.

desert_p21_059.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_059.text: Related water had drawn them to the same town, but each would carry her own claim home.

desert_p21_060.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_060.text: The courtyard lamp repairer asked the older patient whether she minded him working on a rattling shutter at the agreed afternoon hour. She did not, provided he stopped explaining each hammer stroke as if the whole house were his apprentice. He laughed and completed the repair in remarkably little conversation. The improved shutter changed the glare on her mirror. Yue helped the daughter turn the mirror to the new angle, then sat while the patient dictated a brief household letter.

desert_p21_061.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_061.text: It asked after the well rope, complained about the view's former wall and told the keeper not to let the children make syrup from every onion flower. The letter sounded like someone still belonging to a place she could not presently walk through. The niece's paid work made her more protective of her rested time. When a neighbour asked her to lift a washing basin, she declined and offered to move smaller items instead. The neighbour grumbled but accepted. The latch maker had said accuracy improved when workers stopped trying to prove they could carry everything.

desert_p21_062.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_062.text: Bao's gradual shoulder plan gave the statement a physical reason. At the courtyard, the niece counted her small wages against next week's room share and set aside enough for boots later. Her aunt watched and asked whether the boots would have good fastening. The niece said better than her old rush repair, if she could afford the pair she liked.

desert_p21_063.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_063.text: The young worker received notice that his training grant application had passed the first eligibility check. The actual award still required the remaining assessment and the household contribution shown on the form. He was pleased enough to run three steps down the lane, then remembered the dressed finger and stopped waving it in the air. The municipal driver's brother would attend the same assessment after their driver returned from the funded conservation visit. The worker left a note at the receiving yard instead of expecting the man to be in two places at once.

desert_p21_064.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_064.text: Han took the note and put it beneath the actual next expected return date. Bao's first staffed pilot afternoon opened in the grass village after the prepared room passed its conditions. She travelled there on the contracted local service, with her own bounded kit and the village's maintained source arrangement. The trained attendant received names and cleaned the work surface; Bao did the medical assessment. Three ordinary work complaints came through, and one required referral rather than treatment in the small room. The transfer contact answered through the agreed receiving route and the patient went to the municipal clinic.

desert_p21_065.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_065.text: The pilot's value appeared precisely where its limit did: a person was seen, then sent to care the room could not supply. Bao returned tired, carrying actual notes rather than a story of curing a village.

desert_p21_066.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_066.text: Yue met her at the town receiving lane with supper wrapped in a cloth she owned. Bao said the first patient had asked whether opening on two posted days meant illness should also keep appointments. She had answered that urgent problems should use the stated transfer contacts at other times, not wait for her room. The joke had helped the explanation. The attendant had managed the cleaning sequence well and nearly offered a diagnosis once, then corrected herself and called Bao. There would be more teaching. Yue gave her the warm supper.

desert_p21_067.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_067.text: Bao took it in both hands and looked suddenly younger, as though doing the possible part had spent the fear and left ordinary hunger.

desert_p21_068.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p21_068.text: The room worked for its first afternoon, with the referral working where the room ended. I will review the supplies and the missed steps before the next staffed day. I am glad, and I am not declaring it a perfect service because three people came through and the roof stayed dry. That sounds like something Gao would say about a coupling. We are all becoming each other's worst habits. Bring me the soup before I become Du and ask for a historical comparison. Thank you.

desert_p21_069.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p21_069.text: I will return the cloth washed; I know how fiercely you have begun keeping track of borrowed household things.

desert_p21_070.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_070.text: Tuo spent her next recovered walking session buying a plain new staff tip. The old one had worn unevenly enough to irritate her on the town paving. She selected the ordinary ferrule, had it fitted and tested the contact on a safe dry patch. Yue accompanied her without turning the purchase into a desert qualification. The guide said she might take a limited local hire once her clinical review supported it, and would decide by the route rather than the pride attached to her name. She tapped the repaired staff twice. The sound was satisfying.

desert_p21_071.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_071.text: A tool could improve a morning without declaring a whole body ready for every mountain.

desert_p21_072.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_072.text: The patient dictated another letter, this one to her granddaughter in a different town. She omitted the frightening bridge moment and described the bitter plum tree, the mirror and the niece's latch work. Yue asked whether she wanted the clinic follow-up mentioned. She did, in one plain line stating the injury remained supported and care continued. The letter belonged to the woman; the public route report did not. Yue copied it, read it back and made the correction the patient requested. Her handwriting in the last line was more tired than in the first.

desert_p21_073.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_073.text: She sealed the wrapper only after its owner approved the whole page and named the actual carrier to use. Han's mother came to the courtyard with the daughter carrying a small jar of soup. The two older women began by discussing coughs and legs, then swiftly discovered a shared dislike of relatives who whispered in doorways. Han, arriving later, was told to enter or go away. He entered and took the chair offered.

desert_p21_074.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_074.text: The lamp repairer produced an extra cup, the landlord lent a spoon, and the niece found that the house contained a meal without anybody having declared a reception. Yue washed the borrowed cups afterwards under their owners' ordinary arrangement. Warm talk drifted across the court while the plum leaves barely moved.

desert_p21_075.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_075.text: The next conservation note reported supported transport approved for a subset of the relay material under its recorded condition and public custody, with the rest left protected and separately listed. Current drainage observations had also been made from safe points outside. The team remained six adults and four mules, within its planned return window; actual water draws were entered but no final return quantity could yet be claimed. The municipal handling room was ready for the expected arrival. Yue read the note aloud to the patient at her request, leaving private archive details in the proper wrapper.

desert_p21_076.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_076.text: The older woman asked whether the grandmother's story was becoming easier to find. Yue said more of its route was known.

desert_p21_077.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_077.text: The courtyard's review meeting was deliberately brief. The daughter, niece, landlord and social clerk checked the next rent interval, support provision and clinical follow-up date before the initial assistance expired. The patient listened, asked about the mirror's place and agreed to the continued arrangement. An extension from the responsible district provision was approved for its stated term, with household contributions confirmed and a later review scheduled. No one promised perpetual free lodging. No one expected an unfinished historical claim to pay next Tuesday's rent.

desert_p21_078.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_078.text: The clerk left the signed page on the house calendar, where ordinary bills and ordinary care could occupy the same wall. After the meeting Yue sat alone beneath the plum tree for a few minutes. The patient slept inside; the niece had gone to her bounded work session; the daughter was at the bakery. A fallen leaf drifted onto the signed house calendar's wrapper, and Yue moved it away before the ink acquired a stain. She had helped with errands, sheets and cups.

desert_p21_079.speaker: narrator
desert_p21_079.text: Other people had paid rent, made clinical decisions, built a ramp, taken shifts and chosen what they wanted. The court had become a place she could visit and then leave. When the evening bell sounded, she rose, took her habitual pack and went home before somebody's kindness became a reason to stay past the hour she had promised.
